'''Robert Killick-Kendrick''' (20 June 1929 &ndash; 22 October 2011) was a British parasitologist<ref name="RiouxLandau2012">{{cite journal|last1=Rioux|first1=J.A.|last2=Landau|first2=I.|last3=Houin|first3=R.|title=Robert Killick-Kendrick (1929-2011)|journal=Parasite|volume=19|issue=3|year=2012|pages=290–292|issn=1252-607X|doi=10.1051/parasite/2012193290|doi-access=free |pmc=5394826|pmid=23019663}} {{open access}}</ref> with interests in the vectors of infectious diseases, in particular [[Phlebotominae|phlebotomine sandflies]]. His work on malaria, [[trypanosomiasis]], leishmaniasis and other parasitological infections are numerous and diverse. He published more than 300 articles and scientific contributions.

== Education ==

*Master of Philosophy (MPhil)
*1972 - Doctorate (PhD)
*1978 - Doctor of Science (DSc) from the [[University of London]] for his work in [[parasitology]]
*DIC
*FIMLS
*(Hon) [[Royal Entomological Society|FRES]]
*FSB
*CBiol ([[Chartered Biologist]])

== Career ==
Killick-Kendrick was born in Hampton, Middlesex, and educated at [[Woking College#History|Woking Grammar School]]. He left at 16, worked for a year in the Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries in [[Weybridge]], then spent two years in the [[Royal Army Medical Corps]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Robert Killick-Kendrick Obituary|url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2011/dec/23/robert-killick-kendrick-obituary | location=London | work=The Guardian|first1=Ralph|last1=Lainson|first2=John|last2=Baker|date=23 December 2011}}</ref>

In 1949, he started his career in research as a laboratory assistant at the [[London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine]]. From 1955 he worked for eight years in Nigeria investigating [[trypanosomiasis|trypanosome]] infections in humans as well as cattle.<ref>{{cite web|title=In memoriam, Professor Robert Killick-Kendrick 1929–2011|url=https://www.who.int/neglected_diseases/memoriam_robert_killic-kendrick/en/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304050918/http://www.who.int/neglected_diseases/memoriam_robert_killic-kendrick/en/|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 4, 2016|publisher=World Health Organization}}</ref> He once trekked 415 miles (664&nbsp;km) over 28 days, accompanied by a colleague and 28 cattle, to determine where the cattle became infected with trypanosomes. He returned to the London School in 1963 to continue research on malaria parasites with [[Cyril Garnham]] and others. After Garnham's retirement in 1968, he followed him to [[Imperial College London]], where their work on malaria continued.

In 1972, he began investigating [[leishmaniasis]] and its vectors [[sandflies]].<ref>{{cite web|title=About the narrator: Dr KIllick-Kendrick|url=http://www.scalibor.com/about-the-narrator.asp}}</ref><ref name="LawyerKillick-Kendrick2017">{{cite journal|last1=Lawyer|first1=Phillip|last2=Killick-Kendrick|first2=Mireille|last3=Rowland|first3=Tobin|last4=Rowton|first4=Edgar|last5=Volf|first5=Petr|title=Laboratory colonization and mass rearing of phlebotomine sand flies (Diptera, Psychodidae)|journal=Parasite|volume=24|year=2017|pages=42|url= |doi=10.1051/parasite/2017041|doi-access=free |pmc=5687099|pmid=29139377}} {{open access}}</ref> For several years he lived in [[Cévennes]].

In 1988, Killick-Kendrick was named as a member of the World Health Organization Expert Committee on [[Leishmaniasis]] where he was involved in the creation of the 1990 Technical Report Series on the Control of Leishmaniasis, as well as contributed to the 2010 Expert Committee meeting on leishmaniasis.<ref>{{cite web|title=In memoriam, Professor Robert Killick-Kendrick 1929–2011|url=https://www.who.int/neglected_diseases/memoriam_robert_killic-kendrick/en/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304050918/http://www.who.int/neglected_diseases/memoriam_robert_killic-kendrick/en/|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 4, 2016|publisher=World Health Organization}}</ref>

== Honours ==
{
* Honorary Member of the [[Royal Entomological Society]] (in 2005)
* Honorary Member of the [[Società Italiana di Parassitologia]] (in 1991)
* Member of the [[American Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene]]
* Member of the [[Académie des Hauts Cantons]] (in 2008)
* Honorary Member of the [[Turkish Society for Parasitology]] (in 2011){{cn|date=June 2026}}

For his contributions to tropical medicine, Killick-Kendrick received:
* the Sir Rickard Christophers Medal from the [[Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene]] (in 1991)<ref>{{cite web|title=List of past medal holders|url=http://www.rstmh.org/awards/medals/list-past-medal-holders#Christophers|publisher=RSTMH|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110910123308/http://www.rstmh.org/awards/medals/list-past-medal-holders#Christophers|archivedate=2011-09-10}}</ref> 
* the [[Émile Brumpt|Emile Brumpt]] International Prize (in 2007){{cn|date=June 2026}}

== Public engagements ==

Killick-Kendrick acted as the narrator for a series of videos produced by [[Scalibor]] entitled "What's biting my dog?" to explain which parasites affect dogs, and how this can be prevented.<ref>{{cite web|title="What's biting my dog?" Scalibor|url=http://www.scalibor.com/home.asp}}</ref>
